lessons.title: What Would You Like?

items.example: Je voudrais un billet, s'il vous plaît.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a ticket, please.

items.example: J'ai besoin d'un billet pour Paris.
items.exampleMeaning: I need a ticket to Paris.
It's a ticket for Lyon.

items.example: Je voudrais un aller simple pour Lyon.
items.exampleMeaning: I would like a one-way ticket to Lyon.
I would like a return ticket.
Here is my boarding pass.

lessons.tip: Use 'Je voudrais' to politely express what you want. It shows respect and is commonly used in French.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bonjour ! Je voudrais un billet, s'il vous plaît.
dialogue.meaning: Hello! I would like a ticket, please.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Un aller simple ou un aller-retour ?

scenario.partnerRole: A ticket agent at the airport
scenario.brief: You are at the airport. Ask for a ticket to your destination. Be polite and use 's'il vous plaît'.
scenario.goal: You need to ask for a ticket.

lessons.title: Travel Documents

items.exampleMeaning: I have my passport here.
Do you have an ID card?
Where are my documents?
I need to check my documents.
My passport is here.

items.example: Où est le contrôle des passeports ?
items.exampleMeaning: Where is the passport control?

lessons.tip: In France, it's important to have your 'passeport' or 'carte d'identité' ready when traveling. Always check your documents before your trip.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Merci. Je vais vérifier vos documents.
dialogue.meaning: Thank you. I will check your documents.

scenario.brief: You are at the border control. Show your travel documents. Make sure to answer questions politely.
scenario.goal: You need to show your passport and ID.

lessons.title: Asking Questions

items.example: Comment ça marche pour le vol ?
items.exampleMeaning: How does it work for the flight?

items.text: Quel est le numéro de vol ?
items.example: Quel est le numéro de vol pour Paris ?
items.exampleMeaning: What is the flight number to Paris?

items.example: À quelle heure part le vol ?
items.exampleMeaning: At what time does the flight leave?
Where is the boarding gate?
How much is it for the luggage?
Why is the flight delayed?

lessons.tip: Use these phrases to ask questions at the airport. Starting with 'Quel' or 'Où' helps you get specific information.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Quel est le numéro de votre vol ?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: At what time does it leave?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: The gate is on the right.

scenario.brief: You are at the airport. Ask questions about your flight and boarding gate. Use polite language.
scenario.goal: You need to find out information about your flight.

lessons.title: Confirming Information

items.exampleMeaning: Okay, thank you for the information.
I understand now.
It's good, I am ready.

items.example: Merci pour votre aide avec les documents.
items.exampleMeaning: Thank you for your help with the documents.

items.example: Pas de problème, je peux attendre.
items.exampleMeaning: No problem, I can wait.
Everything is clear now.

lessons.tip: Use phrases like 'D'accord' or 'Merci pour votre aide' to confirm understanding and show appreciation. It’s polite and helpful.

scenario.brief: You are at the airport. Confirm details about your flight. Show that you understand and appreciate the help.
scenario.goal: You need to confirm your flight details.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bonjour ! Quel est le numéro de votre vol ?
dialogue.meaning: Hello! What is your flight number?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Okay. At what time does it leave?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: The gate is on the left.

scenario.brief: You are at the airport. Confirm your flight details with the agent. Use questions and polite phrases.
scenario.goal: You need to confirm your flight information and boarding gate.
